entities.name: Anorexia nervosa
observations: Acute illness is associated with widespread cortical thinning; studies report cortical thickness normalizing after weight restoration.

entities.name: PMID:25433902
observations: Cross-sectional study: acute adolescent/young adult females (n=40) had thinning across >85% of cortical surface; long-term recovered group (n=34) had cortical thickness comparable to controls.

entities.name: PMID:26876474
observations: Longitudinal adolescent/young-adult study: after about 3 months and >10% BMI increase, global cortical thickness increased 0.06 mm/month and normalized versus controls in the rescanned cohort.

entities.name: PMID:35025002
observations: Approximately one-year adolescent follow-up: widespread cortical-thickness deficits in acute anorexia nervosa were absent in the weight-recovered follow-up group; hippocampal gray matter and pontine white matter reductions remained.

entities.name: PMID:34479625
observations: Cross-sectional adult study found eight thinner regions in partially restored patients but only one thinner region in weight-restored patients versus controls; regional residual thinning cautions against claiming complete regional recovery.

entities.name: PMID:37876109
observations: After an average 3.5 months of restoration in adolescents, cortical-thickness network modularity improved but network organization remained partly abnormal; this is distinct from global mean cortical thickness.
